expectations.description: Clearly states the evidence is not adequate (no hedging that obscures the answer)
expectations.evidence: Opens unambiguously: 'No, that is not adequate evidence to claim construct validity has been established.'

expectations.description: Mentions that validity is about score interpretation/use, not a property checked off
expectations.evidence: Explicitly states validity 'refers to the degree to which evidence and theory support the interpretation and use of test scores for a specific purpose and population' and that 'you cannot establish validity once and for all.'

expectations.description: Mentions Messick or the 2014 Standards or the unified view of validity
expectations.evidence: Cites 'Standards for Educational and Psychological Testing (AERA/APA/NCME, 2014)' and its five sources of validity evidence framework.

expectations.description: Identifies that one correlation is convergent evidence at most, not full construct validity
expectations.evidence: States 'A single correlation of r = 0.55 between two self-report measures of the same construct is convergent evidence — and not even particularly strong convergent evidence at that.'

expectations.description: Mentions that both measures being self-report introduces common-method variance
expectations.evidence: Dedicates a full section to this: 'the observed correlation is inflated by common-method variance — shared variance attributable to the method of measurement... rather than to the construct itself.'

expectations.description: Names MTMM (multitrait-multimethod) or the trait/method variance distinction
expectations.evidence: Explicitly invokes 'multitrait-multimethod (MTMM) framework,' cites Campbell and Fiske (1959), and discusses the need to separate trait variance from method variance.

expectations.description: Mentions at least two additional sources of validity evidence that would be needed
expectations.evidence: Lists content evidence, internal structure evidence (factor analysis), discriminant evidence, response process evidence, and multi-method measurement as additional sources needed.
